pages.text: $(l)Magnetic Alloy$()$(br)Mix $(item)2 Nickel Ingots$(), $(item)1 Silicon Ingot$() and $(item)2 Steel Ingots$() in a $(item)heated$() basin: you get $(item)2 Magnetic Alloy Ingots$() (15 seconds). Press an ingot to get a $(item)Magnetic Alloy Sheet$(); nine sheets craft a Laminated Magnetic Alloy Block.

$(l)The Polarizer$()$(br)The $(item)Polarizer$() turns a $(item)Magnetic Alloy Ingot$() into a $(item)Magnet$(). Right-click it with the ingot (or feed it with a funnel), then give it power on its $(item)back face$().

$(li)It needs at least $(item)2000 W$(). While charging it is a 30 ohm load, so about $(item)245 V$() is the minimum.$(li)Charging takes $(item)10 seconds$(), then the ingot becomes a magnet. Goggles show the charge.$(li)Right-click with an empty hand to take the magnet out.

$(l)Your first magnet$()$(br)The polarizer needs an $(item)Electric Gauge$(), and the gauge needs a magnet. Since 1.3.0 a hand recipe breaks that loop: a $(item)Magnetic Alloy Ingot$() in the middle, $(item)Blocks of Redstone$() above, left and right of it, and a $(item)Compass$() below. It is expensive on purpose: build a polarizer as soon as you can.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
